purpose: Lanthanum carbonate is used to lower high phosphate levels in your blood, which is a common problem in people with kidney disease who are on dialysis. When your kidneys are not working well, they cannot remove extra phosphate from your body. Keeping phosphate levels under control helps protect your bones and heart.
how_it_works: When you eat food, phosphate is released in your stomach and intestines. Lanthanum carbonate works by grabbing onto that phosphate in your digestive tract before it can be absorbed into your blood. Think of it like a magnet that attracts and traps the phosphate, which then leaves your body in your stool instead of building up in your blood.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, and diarrhea, especially when you first start taking it. Some people also experience constipation or an upset stomach. These symptoms often improve as your body gets used to the medication.
warnings: Always chew the tablets thoroughly before swallowing — do not swallow them whole. Let your doctor know if you have a bowel blockage or any stomach or intestinal problems before taking this medication. This medicine should be taken with or right after meals so it can work properly. Do not take other medications at the same time without checking with your pharmacist, as lanthanum can interfere with how some medicines are absorbed.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 1500 mg per day, divided and taken with meals — for example, 500 mg with each of your three meals. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on your blood phosphate levels. Always chew the tablets completely and take them with food for the best results.
